newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INTERVIEW-Arco coal sale to trigger shakeup.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Arco coal sale to trigger shakeup.

text.p: The decision by United States energy giant Atlantic Richfield Co (ARCO) to quit its worldwide coal business is set to trigger a major shake-up in the Australian state of Queensland's A$4 billion coal industry.

A decision on a public offering or a trade sale for Arco's Australian assets is yet to be made but a float of its three coal mines in central Queensland was possible, Arco Coal Australia told Reuters.

"What we're looking for is a transaction but on the reverse side there is a lot of money in the stockmarket that would make a float attractive," Arco Coal Australia Inc president Bill Wagener said in an interview.
Wagener said offers for the Gordonstone, Curragh and Blair Athol mines will be examined but either way, a sale or float could take up to a year to complete.
The three mines produce about 20 million tonnes of coal and represent about 20 percent of Queensland's total production.
Analysts placed valuations of up to A$500 million on a float of the Gordonstone and Curragh mines, located in the Bowen Basin where a large portion of Australia's coking coal is produced.

With the Blair Athol mine likely to taken by joint venture partner RTZ-CRA Ltd under a pre-emptive agreement, the Gordonstone (coking coal) and Curragh (thermal coal) mines could be worth up to A$600 million as a straight trade sale, said an analyst from Brisbane broking house Wilson HTM Ltd.

The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd had already expressed interest in Gordonstone and Curragh while Shell Australia Ltd, MIM Holdings Ltd and QCT Resources Ltd were all possible buyers, Wilson's Phil Hutchings said.
"Arco has spent about A$700 million on Gordonstone while Blair Athol is one of the best mines in Queensland," he said.
Wagener said the sale of Arco's coal assets would mean the end of the company's presence in Australia.
However, the decision to withdraw from Australia was "strategic" and had nothing to do with underperformance, he said.
"Arco's board, directors and management team's decision was aimed at creating shareholder return and to sharpen the focus on oil and gas and specialty chemicals," Wagener said.
